extracted.intended_audience: owners and operators of CCR units; facility environmental/compliance managers; qualified professional engineers; permitting authorities
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and deadlines for design, operation, groundwater monitoring, closure, post-closure care, and reporting for CCR units and legacy CCR surface impoundments under 40 CFR Part 257.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of liner type (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than April 17, 2018, complete the documentation of liner type as set forth by §257.71(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to owners/operators of inactive CCR surface impoundments; deadline and citation to §257.71(a),(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent identification marker (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than June 16, 2017, place on or immediately adjacent to the CCR unit the permanent identification marker as set forth by §257.73(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadline and citation to §257.73(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Action Plan (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than October 16, 2018, prepare and maintain an Emergency Action Plan as set forth by §257.73(a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement to prepare and maintain EAP; citation to §257.73(a)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: History of construction (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than April 17, 2018, compile a history of construction as set forth by §257.73(b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document construction history per cited provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial hazard potential classification and stability assessments (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than April 17, 2018, complete the initial hazard potential classification, structural stability, and safety factor assessments as set forth by §257.73(a)(2), (b), (d), (e), and (f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete specified geotechnical/hazard assessments by date; citations provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial CCR fugitive dust control plan (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than April 18, 2017, prepare the initial CCR fugitive dust control plan as set forth in §257.80(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating-criteria requirement and deadline; citation to §257.80(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial inflow design flood control system plan (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than April 17, 2018, prepare the initial inflow design flood control system plan as set forth in §257.82(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating-criteria requirement and citation to §257.82(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspections by a qualified person (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than April 18, 2017, initiate the inspections by a qualified person as set forth by §257.83(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating-criteria inspection initiation requirement and date; citation to §257.83(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial annual inspection by a qualified professional engineer (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than July 19, 2017, complete the initial annual inspection by a qualified professional engineer as set forth by §257.83(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating-criteria requirement and deadline; citation to §257.83(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater monitoring compliance (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than April 17, 2019, comply with groundwater monitoring requirements set forth in §§257.90(b) and 257.94(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owners/operators must meet the cited groundwater monitoring requirements by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial groundwater monitoring and corrective action report (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than August 1, 2019, prepare the initial groundwater monitoring and corrective action report as set forth in §257.90(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report preparation deadline and citation to §257.90(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial written closure plan (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than April 17, 2018, prepare an initial written closure plan as set forth in §257.102(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closure plan preparation requirement and citation to §257.102(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial written post-closure care plan (inactive CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than April 17, 2018, prepare an initial written post-closure care plan as set forth in §257.104(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-closure care plan preparation requirement and citation to §257.104(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy CCR applicability report (deadline and placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must prepare an applicability report for each unit no later than Friday, November 8, 2024; the report is prepared when placed in the facility operating record per §257.105(k)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and when the report is considered prepared (operating record placement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum contents of applicability report (legacy CCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: At a minimum the applicability report must contain: (A) owner/operator name and address with business phone and email; (B) name associated with the unit; (C) identifying information including facility figure, unit location, facility address, latitude/longitude; (D) state-assigned identification number if any; (E) description of current site conditions including current use of inactive facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit list (A–E) of required information to identify the legacy CCR surface impoundment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification statement for applicability report
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators must certify the applicability report with the specified penalty-of-law statement signed by the owner/operator or authorized representative (statement provided verbatim in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification language required; must be signed; attests to truth/accuracy and awareness of penalties for false statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to EPA of CCR website and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must notify the Agency of establishment of the facility's CCR website and the applicability of the rule using procedures in §257.107(a) via the 'contact us' form on EPA's CCR website (deadline: no later than Nov 8, 2024 for applicability reports and extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for notification; tied to report/extension timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability extension for field investigation to determine free liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators may secure additional time (maximum 18 months, in 6-month increments) solely to determine through a field investigation whether the unit contains both CCR and liquids by preparing an applicability extension report as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions are limited to 18 months total, must be supported by successive applicability extension reports, and adjust compliance timeframes for later requirements by the length of extension(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability extension report basic content
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicability extension report must include: the information specified in paragraph (f)(1)(i)(A)–(C) (owner/operator contact and identification info), a statement that existing info is insufficient to determine presence of free liquids, and details of a written field investigation work plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the minimum components of an extension request before the detailed workplan requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field investigation work plan required elements (applicability extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: The written field investigation work plan must include: (i) detailed approach to characterize physical/topographic/geologic/hydrogeologic/hydraulic properties and how used to investigate free liquids; (ii) methods/tools to determine presence of free liquids, rationale, implementation, spatial resolution; (iii) description of how groundwater elevations will be determined and evaluated relative to unit sides/bottom, with spatial resolution; (iv) plan for evaluating stormwater flow/drainage/infiltration with topographic map showing surface flow and pertinent features; (v) estimated timeline to complete workplan and determine if unit contains free liquids; (vi) narrative how results will determine presence of free liquids; (vii) narrative describing anticipated problems and contingency actions/timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive, multi-part list (i–vii) specifying what the work plan must cover to justify extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PE certification of field investigation work plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner/operator must obtain a written certification from a qualified professional engineer stating that the field investigation work plan meets the requirements of paragraph (f)(1)(iii)(A)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualified professional engineer must certify the adequacy of the work plan in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing/sequence rules for applicability extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial applicability extension report must be prepared no later than Nov 8, 2024; subsequent extension reports no later than 6 months after the preceding extension report; the owner/operator has prepared the applicability extension report when placed in the facility's operating record per §257.105(k)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines for submitting extension reports and when they are considered prepared (operating record placement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions if free liquids are found during extension investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: If owner/operator determines unit contains free liquids during implementation of the workplan, they must cease operating under the extension provisions and prepare the applicability report required by paragraph (f)(1) within 14 days; comply with requirements under paragraphs (f)(2)–(5) under new timeframes adjusted by extension length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate cessation of extension-based status and prompt preparation of full applicability report with adjusted timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification if unit does not contain both CCR and liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: If owner/operator determines unit does not contain both CCR and liquids during workplan implementation, they must prepare a notification stating the field investigation concluded and the unit does not meet the definition of a legacy CCR surface impoundment; the notification is prepared when placed in the operating record per §257.105(k)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome notification procedure and when it is considered prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default if field investigation not completed in time
rubrics_metrics.description: If owner/operator does not complete the field investigation within the extension timeframes (max 18 months secured in 6-month increments), the unit shall be considered a legacy CCR surface impoundment and must comply with requirements under paragraphs (f)(2)–(5) pursuant to the timeframes in paragraph (f)(1)(iii)(E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to complete investigation results in being treated as legacy subject to full requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy design criteria deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must, except as noted for incised or small units, meet multiple design deadlines (examples include: place permanent identification marker by Jan 8, 2025; compile history of construction by Feb 9, 2026; complete initial hazard classification and assessments by May 8, 2026; prepare and maintain EAP by May 8, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Series of date-specific design requirements for legacy units with exceptions for incised or small units; citations to §257.73 subparts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy operating criteria deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must meet operating deadlines including: prepare initial CCR fugitive dust control plan by Nov 8, 2024; prevent unknowing/unauthorized entry by Nov 8, 2024; initiate inspections by qualified person by Nov 8, 2024; complete initial annual P.E. inspection by Feb 10, 2025; prepare initial inflow design flood control plan by May 8, 2026; prepare initial annual fugitive dust control report by Jan 8, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed list of operating requirements with specific dates and citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy groundwater monitoring system installation and program development
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than May 10, 2027, owners/operators must: (i) install the groundwater monitoring system required by §257.91; (ii) develop the groundwater sampling and analysis program including selection of statistical procedures per §257.93.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Installation and program development deadlines and citations to §§257.91 and 257.93.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy groundwater monitoring data compliance and detection monitoring initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: By May 10, 2027 owners/operators must: (A) initiate detection monitoring to include obtaining a minimum of eight independent samples for each background and downgradient well per §257.94(b); (B) begin evaluating data for statistically significant increases over background for appendix III constituents per §257.94; (C) begin evaluating data for statistically significant levels over groundwater protection standards for appendix IV constituents per §257.95.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific monitoring program actions, sample minimums, and statistical evaluation requirements with citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial groundwater monitoring and corrective action report (legacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than January 31, 2027, prepare the initial groundwater monitoring and corrective action report as set forth in §257.90(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report preparation deadline and citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy closure and post-closure plan deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in §257.102(g), owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must prepare an initial written closure plan and initial written post-closure care plan no later than Monday, November 8, 2027, as set forth in §257.102(b) and §257.104(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadline for preparing closure and post-closure care plans for legacy units with citation references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure certification for units closed prior to Nov 8, 2024
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments that completed closure by removal prior to Nov 8, 2024 must, no later than Nov 8, 2024, complete a closure certification including supporting information: type/volume of CCR prior to closure; methods and documentation verifying complete removal and post-removal sampling; methods/documentation verifying decontamination of areas; documentation groundwater affected has achieved protection standards; documentation that groundwater monitoring system met representativeness and capability requirements (i–vii), and last sample used to document standards was collected no earlier than one year prior to initiation of closure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive list (1–6 and subitems i–vii) of evidence and monitoring system capability documentation required for closure-by-removal certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative to closure certification: two-event groundwater monitoring demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: If unable to complete closure-by-removal certification by the due date, owner/operator may elect to conduct groundwater monitoring under §§257.90–257.95 to demonstrate no exceedances of groundwater protection standards; must complete requirements in paragraph (h)(1) (notification of intent by Nov 8, 2024; conduct at least two consecutive sampling events demonstrating no exceedances; complete closure-by-removal certification by May 8, 2028) to avoid further requirements under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an alternative compliance path contingent on monitoring results and additional deadlines; failure to meet it triggers corrective action path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if monitoring path fails or SSLs detected
rubrics_metrics.description: If owner/operator does not meet the monitoring demonstration requirements by May 8, 2028, or if one or more appendix IV constituents are detected at statistically significant levels above the groundwater protection standard, they must follow a list of subsequent compliance actions (corrective action per §257.102(c)(2), permanent marker within 8 months, applicability report within 6 months, facility evaluation within 33 months, fugitive dust if new CCR units discovered within 6 months, groundwater requirements within 48 months, initial written closure plan within 54 months, initial post-closure plan within 54 months, initiate closure within 60 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates staged deadlines and requirements triggered by detection of contamination or failure to meet monitoring demonstration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited obligations for legacy units closed or meeting standards before Nov 8, 2024
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators that completed closure in accordance with §257.102(d) or meet §257.101(g) prior to Nov 8, 2024 must only: prepare applicability report; prevent unknowing/unauthorized entry; place permanent ID marker; compile history of construction; prepare initial fugitive dust plan and report; install groundwater monitoring system; develop sampling/analysis program; initiate detection monitoring and statistical evaluations; include completed closure documentation in applicability report; prepare initial post-closure care plan; conduct post-closure care; and comply with recordkeeping/notification/website requirements (§§257.105–257.107).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduced set of continuing obligations and documentation for pre- Nov 8, 2024 compliant closures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping, notification, and internet requirements for legacy units
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators of legacy CCR surface impoundments must comply with the recordkeeping requirements in §257.105(k), notification requirements in §257.106(k), and internet requirements in §257.107(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references to recordkeeping/notification/website provisions that must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner/operator initiation of closure (legacy CCR surface impoundment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (g), no later than Monday, May 8, 2028, an owner/operator of a legacy CCR surface impoundment must initiate closure of the unit in accordance with §257.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandated initiation of closure by specified date unless deferral applies; must include statement in notification if closing under this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owner/operator initiation of closure (CCR management unit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraphs (g) and (h), no later than Tuesday, May 8, 2029, an owner/operator of a CCR management unit must initiate closure in accordance with §257.102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate initiation deadline for CCR management units and requirement to include a statement in the §257.102(g) notification if closing under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral to permitting for substantially equivalent regulatory closures
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators need not demonstrate compliance with §257.102(c) or (d) if they demonstrate closure met standards (g)(1)–(6): regulatory authority oversaw/approved closure under enforceable requirement; regulatory authority required/conducted a site-specific risk assessment; documented groundwater monitoring system and monitoring that meets capabilities (i–iv); documented closed unit meets either §257.60 or §257.102(d)(2)(i); include the specified signed certification statement in facility evaluation or applicability report; and submit permit application documentation for closure equivalency determination at permitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements to document oversight, risk assessment, monitoring capability, performance standard equivalency, certification statement inclusion, and permitting submission/ EPA/State review for equivalency determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure equivalency determination and permitting process
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must submit a permit application with sufficient information (including groundwater contaminant data) to demonstrate §257.102 standards have been met; EPA will review and determine equivalency and may issue a permit requiring post-closure requirements or require a complete permit application and specific requirements if standards are not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes EPA/Participating State Director review and possible outcomes after permit application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral for CCR management units under critical infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator of a CCR management unit beneath critical infrastructure need not initiate closure until the infrastructure is no longer needed, EPA/Participating State Director determines closure necessary to avoid reasonable probability of adverse effects, or facility closure/decommissioning occurs; owners/operators of CCR management units under active disposal units must demonstrate compliance with either §257.60 or §257.102(d)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows deferral for critical infrastructure with required demonstration of performance standard compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure methods allowable (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure of a CCR unit must be completed either by leaving the CCR in place with a final cover system or by removal of the CCR and decontamination of the CCR unit, as described in paragraphs (b)–(j). Retrofit of CCR surface impoundment must follow paragraph (k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the two fundamental closure approaches and reference to retrofit rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of written closure plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Written closure plan must describe steps necessary to close the CCR unit consistent with recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices and must include at minimum: (i) narrative description of how unit will be closed; (ii) procedures for removal and decontamination if removal chosen; (iii) description of final cover system and installation methods and discussion of how it will achieve performance standards if leaving CCR in place; (iv) estimate of maximum CCR inventory ever on-site; (v) estimate of largest area ever requiring final cover; (vi) schedule for completing all activities necessary to satisfy closure criteria, including major milestones and estimated timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed list (i–vi) of required elements for the closure plan and requirement to be consistent with good engineering practices; if estimated closure time exceeds timeframes in paragraph (f)(1), plan must include site-specific info to support any time extension sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframes for preparing initial written closure plan
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) Existing CCR landfills and surface impoundments: no later than October 17, 2016; (ii) New CCR landfills/surface impoundments and any lateral expansion: no later than date of initial receipt of CCR; (iii) CCR management units: no later than November 8, 2028 (except paragraph (b)(2)(v) exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific deadlines by unit type and when the written closure plan is considered completed (placed in facility operating record per §257.105(i)(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure documentation for CCR management units closed prior to Nov 8, 2024
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators that completed closure in accordance with §257.102(d) prior to Nov 8, 2024 or meet §257.101(g) must include in the facility evaluation report (§257.75) information on the completed closure along with supporting documentation demonstrating the closure meets performance standards in §257.102(d) or §257.101(g) standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement to include prior closure documentation in facility evaluation reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment triggers and timing for written closure plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator may amend the initial or subsequent written closure plan at any time. They must amend whenever: (A) there is an operational change that would substantially affect the plan; or (B) unanticipated events necessitate revision. Amend at least 60 days prior to a planned change, or no later than 60 days after an unanticipated event; if revised after closure activities have commenced, amend no later than 30 days following the triggering event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when amendments are required and strict timelines for making amendments depending on whether closure activities have commenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification or approval of written closure plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator must obtain written certification from a qualified professional engineer or approval from the Participating State Director or EPA (where EPA is the permitting authority) that the initial and any amendment of the written closure plan meets the requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates P.E. certification or official approval for initial plans and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure by removal completion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Closure by removal is complete when CCR has been removed; any areas affected by releases have been removed or decontaminated; and groundwater monitoring concentrations of appendix IV constituents do not exceed groundwater protection standards in §257.95(h). Removal/decontamination includes removing CCR mixed with soils and CCR in berms/liners/structures, and removing/decontaminating all areas affected by releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines completion of removal and required scope of removal/decontamination activities and the groundwater standard check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete removal during active life requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Within timeframes in paragraph (f), owner/operator must: (i) complete removal and decontamination of all affected areas; (ii) document that paragraph (c) standards have been met, including groundwater monitoring showing no constituents detected at statistically significant levels above standards for either two consecutive monitoring events or three years per §257.98(c); (iii) obtain completion of closure certification or approval required by paragraph (f)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the documentation and monitoring outcomes required to demonstrate completion when removal is done during the active life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial removal with post-closure groundwater corrective action option
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator may complete removal and decontamination except for groundwater corrective action during active life and complete groundwater corrective action during post-closure by: (i) documenting removal of CCR and affected areas within timeframes in paragraph (f); (ii) within those timeframes, begin implementation of remedy selected per §257.97 so all components are constructed/operating unless owner/operator documents meeting §§257.96–257.98 and inability to extend active life until remedy implementation consistent with §257.102(f); (iii) complete groundwater corrective action as a post-closure care requirement as specified in §257.104(g); (iv) amend written closure and post-closure care plans; (v) obtain completion certification/approval as required; (vi) record deed notation as required by paragraph (i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an alternative sequence allowing groundwater corrective action during post-closure, with multiple procedural and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: General performance standard when leaving CCR in place
rubrics_metrics.description: When leaving CCR in place, closure must at minimum: (i) control, minimize or eliminate to the maximum extent feasible post-closure infiltration of liquids into the waste and releases of CCR, leachate, or contaminated run-off to ground/surface waters or atmosphere; (ii) preclude probability of future impoundment of water, sediment, or slurry; (iii) include measures providing major slope stability to prevent sloughing or movement of the final cover system during closure and post-closure; (iv) minimize need for further maintenance; and (v) be completed in the shortest amount of time consistent with recognized and generally accepted good engineering practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five-part performance standard describing required outcomes and design objectives for in-place closures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drainage and stabilization prior to final cover
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to installing the final cover system, (i) free liquids must be eliminated by removing liquid wastes or solidifying remaining wastes and residues; and (ii) remaining wastes must be stabilized sufficient to support the final cover system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two mandatory pre-final-cover requirements to eliminate free liquids and stabilize wastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final cover system (start of requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to install a final cover system designed in accordance with paragraph (d)(3) (text begins here; detailed final cover requirements follow in subsequent provisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that final cover system design/installation requirements are specified in the next section (d)(3).
